hints: Apply the factor theorem: set $p\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 0$ to get a linear equation connecting $a$ and $b$.
Use the remainder theorem: calculate $p(4)$ and $p(2)$ and solve $p(4) = 3p(2)$ simultaneously with the first equation.
walkthrough:
Apply the factor theorem: since $(2x + 1)$ is a factor of $p(x) = 4x^3 + ax^2 + 5x + b$, we have $p\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 0$:
$$4\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^3 + a\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 + 5\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + b = 0$$
$$4\left(-\dfrac{1}{8}\right) + a\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right) - \dfrac{5}{2} + b = 0$$
$$-\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{a}{4} - \dfrac{5}{2} + b = 0$$
$$-3 + \dfrac{a}{4} + b = 0 \implies \dfrac{a}{4} + b = 3 \implies a + 4b = 12 \quad [1]$$

Calculate the remainder when $p(x)$ is divided by $(x - 4)$ using the remainder theorem:
$$p(4) = 4(4)^3 + a(4)^2 + 5(4) + b = 4(64) + 16a + 20 + b = 256 + 16a + 20 + b = 16a + b + 276$$

Calculate the remainder when $p(x)$ is divided by $(x - 2)$ using the remainder theorem:
$$p(2) = 4(2)^3 + a(2)^2 + 5(2) + b = 4(8) + 4a + 10 + b = 32 + 4a + 10 + b = 4a + b + 42$$
